relations.rationale: As head judge/leader, Jun setting the pace fits with being the leading figure of the group.
Jun being head judge has no bearing on weather conditions.
Arriving later and being out of breath from jogging the last stretch are consistent, suggesting Dara rushed to catch up.
Dara's late arrival has no logical connection to the group pausing at a stream later.
Dara's arrival time is unrelated to the number of teams.
Dara showing up late has no bearing on the group's overall satisfaction at the end of the day.
Dara being out of breath from jogging has no relation to who brought the first-aid kit.
Eli's tallness directly explains why his height was useful for spotting trail markers.
Eli's height has no bearing on the group pausing at a stream.
Eli's usefulness for spotting markers is unrelated to the specific description of the trail's terrain.
Eli's height utility for spotting markers has no connection to the group settling into tents by evening.
Yara bringing a first-aid kit is unrelated to the trail's terrain description.
Both show Yara being responsible and prepared, so bringing the first-aid kit supports the idea she was attentive to group needs like timing.
Jun taking a wrong turn near the visitor center would plausibly cause him to arrive last.

Jun arriving last is contradicted by the claim that he still made it before the group set off, since 'arrived last' implies he was the final one, but this doesn't preclude arriving before departure; however, 'arrived last' could still allow him to arrive before others left, so these are compatible rather than contradictory.
Jun arriving last has no direct bearing on whether he set the pace afterward.
Jun's arrival order is unrelated to the number of teams.
Jun arriving last has no connection to the group's later reaction to gathering clouds.

Taking a wrong turn suggests a delay, but the claim that he still made it before the group set off shows he compensated for that delay, making it a supporting circumstance rather than a contradiction.
Jun's wrong turn is unrelated to Yara's time-tracking behavior.
